title: A cookie the extension wrote for itself is unserialized as trusted object state on every request, with no class restriction
index_line: T-0069 · EXEC · the CacheWarmer cookie feeds PHP's native unserialize() on every storefront request, unauthenticated; Magento's shipped classes complete the gadget chain · php · corroborated
invariant_violated: A cookie the extension itself writes was treated as trustworthy state from a peer component. Cookie values are client bytes: the plugin ran them through native unserialize(), choosing no class restriction, on every storefront request — authenticated or not.

mechanism.does: any storefront request carries the extension's cookie; the value is fully attacker-controlled (marker + base64)
the plugin strips the marker and base64-decodes the payload on every request — warmer traffic is not required
the decoded bytes reach PHP's native unserialize() with no allowed-classes argument: the attacker names the classes instantiated
magic methods on classes the platform and its dependencies already ship fire the gadget chain (Monolog handlers observed in the wild)
the chain reaches command execution — one cookie, no authentication, no admin session, no config toggle

source.http.cookie.value: the CacheWarmer cookie — written by the extension for its crawler, read by it on every request

guard.none.value: no authentication, no admin session, no config toggle — and no allowed-classes restriction on the unserialize call

sink.deser.native.value: PHP native unserialize() on client bytes

gadget.magic-method.value: destruct/wakeup gadgets from classes Magento and its dependencies already ship (Monolog\Handler\* observed in live payloads)

preconditions.expr: a cookie path reaches native unserialize() with no second (allowed_classes) argument
the extension is present below its fixed version (often bundled inside other vendor packages, not directly installed)
the storefront answers and accepts the cookie on ordinary pages

success: a single crafted cookie yields command execution with no authentication
request signature: CacheWarmer cookie whose base64 payload starts with serialized-object markers (Tz/Qz/Yt) — observed live since disclosure
failure_like: unserialize called with allowed_classes rejects unknown class names
false_positive: finding unserialize() is not the finding — this platform's gadget inventory is public and deterministic, but the chain must still be shown to fire
a WAF blocking serialized-object cookies is a mitigation, not absence of the bug

hazards: every 'the client echoes back state we handed them' channel: cookies, cache keys, signed-but-not-encrypted tokens — the extension trusted its own vocabulary
the gadget inventory is the dependency tree: Monolog ships with thousands of installs, making exploitation deterministic rather than blind (contrast T-0007)
bundled distribution hides the surface: merchants ran the warmer without ever installing it directly (~6,000 stores ran vendor extensions)
python/pickle and ruby/Marshal cookie paths are the same mechanism with different encodings
non_transfers: unserialize sites with allowed_classes or signed-and-verified state
stores without the extension or past 1.11.12

evidence.target: Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer for Magento 2 < 1.11.12 (CVE-2026-45247, CVSS 3.1 9.8; actively exploited)

provenance.corroborates: the finder's disclosure: CacheWarmer cookie reaches native unserialize() with no class restriction on every storefront request; warmer session-state design; gadget chains from Magento/Monolog classes; CWE-502; fix 1.11.12; detection signature CacheWarmer: + base64 serialized objects
